result.summary: Updates Bitcoin Core's logging macros (`LogError`, `LogWarning`, `LogInfo`, `LogDebug`, `LogTrace`) to accept optional context arguments representing target logger instances, custom formatters, and categories. Macro expansion is consolidated under a new `LOG_EMIT` macro that performs compile-time argument checks, enforces category rules per log level, and avoids unnecessary formatting work when logging is disabled. Rate limiting configuration is moved to an `Options` structure passed through logging hooks.
result.problem: All log macros write to a single global logger instance, which forces consumers of `libbitcoinkernel` to share global log state and prevents isolated logging across separate contexts. Subsystems needing custom message formatting or prefixes (such as wallet names handled via `WalletLogPrintf`) cannot use standard log level macros.
evidence: PR description: "Having a single global log stream works very well for `bitcoind` and will not change. But it limits functionality of libbitcoinkernel, forcing all potential users of the library, including applications written in different languages and running in different environments (like jupyter notebooks) to use shared global state and not be able to do things like get an isolated log trace from one operation."
Commit 6292d61b55: "Unnecessary `strprintf` calls are now skipped when logging is disabled... could speed up fuzz tests calling functions which log."
Commit f5737f0478: adds tests verifying that `Info` and higher severity messages preserve argument side-effect evaluation even if logging is disabled, addressing review feedback from #34374.
result.scope_notes: Part of a PR stack based on #34778. The non-base commits are specifically f48f450b1b8, dc9a4f94f3e, and eea210b6420.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial conceptual changes; the commits remain based on #34778 and implement context arguments and compile-time macro validation.
result.card: Extends the core logging macros to accept optional context arguments, allowing log messages to specify distinct logger instances, metadata, and custom formatters. This addresses libbitcoinkernel's limitation of requiring a shared global logger stream and provides the infrastructure needed to deprecate subsystem-specific logging wrappers like WalletLogPrintf. Author notes this unblocks independent log stream management in kernel PR 30342 and wallet PR 30343. This PR is based on PR 34778.

risk.why: A macro expansion or compile-time check bug in logging utility code would cause compilation errors, formatting failures, or missed log lines, but does not risk consensus, validation state, or node persistence.
